brief:
Palestinian comedians are increasingly turning to comedy as a tool to narrate their experiences of occupation, displacement, and conflict, the Guardian reported. UK-based Palestinian performer Sami Abu Wardeh is among those using the Edinburgh festival stage to process and share stories through humor, treating comedy as essential during the Gaza war—a subject many avoid discussing altogether.

The approach reflects a broader strategy among Palestinian artists to engage audiences on difficult subjects that typically remain off-limits in public conversation. For these performers, humor serves simultaneously as a personal coping mechanism and a means of communicating narratives often marginalized in mainstream discourse. The growing wave of Palestinian performers demonstrates how comedy has become a vehicle for both emotional survival and cultural voice.

title: Palestinian comedian uses humor to address Gaza war, occupation
